copy.gary: I've been wandering Indy parks and I still find something new on most visits, like the Ruins at Holliday Park or the conservatory at Garfield Park on a cold afternoon.
copy.description: Check in at every Indianapolis, Indiana park you visit, collect stamps and badges, rate your favorites and explore with your Park Pals.

motifs.name: Monument Circle
motifs.blurb: The Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument stands at the very center of Indianapolis, on Monument Circle.

motifs.name: Racing capital
motifs.blurb: Every May the Indianapolis 500 fills the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, nicknamed the Brickyard.

motifs.name: The Ruins
motifs.blurb: The Ruins at Holliday Park hold three huge statues saved from New York City's St. Paul Building when it was torn down.

motifs.name: Garfield Park Conservatory
motifs.blurb: Garfield Park, the city's oldest park, has a glass conservatory full of tropical plants beside its sunken gardens.

motifs.name: The White River
motifs.blurb: The White River winds through Indianapolis past Holliday, Broad Ripple and Riverside parks.

motifs.name: Eagle Creek
motifs.blurb: Eagle Creek Park, on the northwest side, is one of the largest city parks in the country, with a reservoir, trails and a nature center.
